clue.text: Clumsy person, terribly old, boarding helicopter

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly and messily, so the letters come out jumbled
a passenger boarding a craft goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: chopper is the informal word for a helicopter
the three letters of old, rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly klutz climbs awkwardly aboard a helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a big-footed, lumbering oaf who trips over things, so it names an awkward individual.

clue.text: Youngster going over a sugar-producing island

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child travels to a Caribbean island famous for its cane fields.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece going over another sits above it, so the youngster comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba has long been one of the world's major growers and exporters of cane, its economy built on that crop.

clue.text: Caught in excessively noisy environment, become dull

indicators.note: an environment is what surrounds something, so the noisy phrase wraps around the other piece

parts.note: over means too, excessively
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a direct synonym

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a deafening place feels their senses grow dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught in' looks like the start of the scene, but caught is just the cricket letter, and 'environment' does the surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcloud is to cover with cloud and so grow dark or gloomy, losing brightness.

clue.text: She helped mate malamutes initially, rocking Herts town

indicators.note: rocking shakes things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: malamutes are sled dogs; only their first letter is used

explanation.surface: A woman assists in breeding sled dogs, and the whole affair shakes up a county town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the standard abbreviation for Hertfordshire, a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemel Hempstead is a large new town in Hertfordshire, north-west of London.

clue.text: Winged horse, — quiet. say, like you and me

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
e.g. means for example, as say does
as means in the manner of
the pronoun covering the speaker and the listener

explanation.surface: A mythical flying horse is described as calm, just like the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is the flying steed of Greek myth, born from Medusa and ridden by Bellerophon.

clue.text: Set aside weapon in English rescue boat

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other, between its letters

parts.note: standard abbreviation
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm
Noah's ark saved its passengers from the flood

explanation.surface: A gun is stowed aboard an English lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The weapon goes inside E plus ARK, between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds or items is to reserve them for a particular purpose, putting them by.

clue.text: Argument suitable to be backed with force

indicators.note: backing up means moving in the opposite direction, so the word reads right to left

parts.note: fit means suitable
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A dispute that ought to be settled by strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel or squabble, usually between friends or lovers.

clue.text: OT patriarch's account supporting another

indicators.note: in a down clue a support holds things up from beneath, so the word before it is placed second, at the bottom

parts.note: another account: an ISA is a British Individual Savings Account
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An Old Testament forefather's story backs up a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath. 'Another' means another account, and an ISA is a tax-free savings account in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham and father of Jacob, is one of the three Hebrew patriarchs of Genesis.

clue.text: Self-employed person in country with right to catch fish

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: an example of a country
standard abbreviation
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A freelancer abroad is entitled to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: FRANCE plus R makes FRANCER, and the eel goes in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelancer sells work to various clients rather than being on one company's payroll.

clue.text: Work on the school map somehow: it's used to examine pupils

indicators.note: somehow says the letters get there by some unspecified rearrangement

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher labours over a classroom map as a tool for checking pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: With the school in the surface, pupils look like schoolchildren; they are the openings in the iris.
explanation.definitionFit: An ophthalmoscope is the instrument an optician shines into the eye to inspect the retina through the pupil.

clue.text: River adopted by ray — and another fish

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ray of light is a beam
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A ray takes in a river, then a second fish appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' sets up a fish, which makes 'another fish' read naturally, but here the ray is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The bream is a deep-bodied freshwater or sea fish, so it is one more fish after the ray.

clue.text: Good Yankee soldiers overturned plot primarily endangering aircraft

parts.note: standard abbreviation
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, which in an across clue means read backwards

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
a plot is a plan or scheme

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter only

explanation.surface: Decent American troops thwarted a scheme threatening a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyroplane is a rotorcraft whose unpowered rotor spins in the airflow, also called an autogyro.

clue.text: Churchy NW town originally advertised in sprawling italics

parts.note: Eccles is a town near Manchester in north-west England, known for its currant cakes

indicators.note: in sets one piece inside the other
sprawling suggests letters spread untidily out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter only

explanation.surface: A northern town's advert appears in sloping type, with a churchy flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled italics letters take the A inside before their final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastical relates to the Christian church or its clergy, so it is a formal word for churchy.

clue.text: Perplex clergy, producing cleaning requisite

parts.note: to floor someone is to baffle them
the cloth is the clergy collectively, as in a man of the cloth

explanation.surface: Puzzling the priests results in a handy cleaning item.
explanation.definitionFit: A floorcloth is a rag used for wiping and mopping floors, a basic household cleaning item.

clue.text: Female with pride in Sir Tristram's birthplace, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Lyonesse is the legendary drowned land off Cornwall where Tristram of Arthurian legend was born

explanation.surface: A proud woman hails from a legendary knight's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' looks like self-esteem, but it is the collective noun for a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: The lioness is the female lion, and lions live in social groups called prides.

clue.text: Family eating pigmeat finally suffers wind in Egypt

indicators.note: something eating food takes it inside, so the piece is enclosed

parts.note: kin are relatives
ham is cured meat from a pig

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word after it

parts.note: the last letter only

explanation.surface: A household tucks into pork and ends up with digestive trouble in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at flatulence after a meal; the wind is a weather system.
explanation.definitionFit: The khamsin is a hot, dry, dusty southerly that blows across Egypt in spring from the Sahara.

clue.text: Grim job, getting supporter on board!

parts.note: stern means severe or grim
a post is a position of employment

explanation.surface: A dreary role is acquiring a backer on the committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a company board; here it means aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternpost is the upright timber at a ship's rear that holds up the rudder, a structural support on a vessel.

clue.text: Complex man's big wordbook I dine over

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary, the biggest English dictionary
taken as written

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read back to front

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper

explanation.surface: A complicated fellow has a huge dictionary and eats out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex man' looks like a complicated person, but it is the figure who gave his name to Freud's complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus is the Theban king of Greek myth after whom Freud named the Oedipus complex.

clue.text: Second row about Kentucky's visible horizon

indicators.note: about means around, so these pieces surround the state abbreviation

parts.note: standard abbreviation
postal abbreviation for the US state
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A further rank surrounds Kentucky's view to the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The skyline is the outline where land or buildings meet the sky, as seen from a viewpoint.

clue.text: Take part in dog show, perhaps, but arrive without dog?

definitions.text: Take part in dog show, perhaps

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: You might enter a dog show, yet turn up without any dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking; here it carries its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to enter a contest, and a dog show is one such contest, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Hawks catching last of sluggish birds

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside

parts.note: to hawk is to clear the throat noisily

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter only

explanation.surface: Birds of prey snatch the slowest of a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawks' wants to be the predators and the definition; it is the verb for clearing one's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Choughs are crows with red legs and curved red bills, found on sea cliffs and mountains.

clue.text: Simple rustics in America kept by state money

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

indicators.note: what is kept by something is held inside it

parts.note: coins are money
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Unsophisticated farm folk in the US are funded by government cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Country cousins are unworldly relatives from rural areas, naive visitors to the town.

clue.text: Stand erect and extremely unbowed outside animal enclosure

indicators.note: outside puts these letters around the other piece
extremely points to the two extreme letters, first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters
a pen holds livestock

explanation.surface: Someone stands tall and defiant outside a pen of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to set it on its end, turning it upright.

clue.text: Muntjac, possibly, bringing up grass

indicators.note: bringing something up in a down clue lifts it from bottom to top, so it reads upwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands

explanation.surface: A small deer, perhaps, is chewing up grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The muntjac is a small Asian species of deer, now common in English woodland, hence possibly.

clue.text: Performing stage work in simple key, including tango

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one letter goes inside the rest

parts.note: an opera is a work for the stage
taken as written
G is a key with a single sharp, a simple one to play in
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A musical show is being put on in an easy key, featuring a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The tango letter goes in after the stage work, before 'in' and the key.
explanation.definitionFit: Operating means functioning or working, as a performing machine or organisation does.

clue.text: Bracing air a specified person associated with Australia

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
one means a particular person, as in the one I mean

explanation.surface: Fresh sea breezes are linked with a certain Aussie.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used loosely for fresh, invigorating seaside air, thought to be good for health.

clue.text: Fell making twitcher's shelter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an animal's skin or pelt
second meaning: a screened hut for watching wildlife

explanation.surface: A hillside provides cover for a birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a northern English hill or the past tense of fall; it is the old word for an animal skin. A twitcher is a keen birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is both a raw animal pelt and a camouflaged hut from which birds are observed.

clue.text: Recently recruited compiler digesting Liberal bulletin

parts.note: a new recruit has just joined

indicators.note: digesting means taking something in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a crossword compiler is its setter
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A new puzzle setter absorbs a political party's circular.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsletter is a regular printed or emailed report sent to members of a group.
